<reason>B established a workable boundary: liability for an operator’s proven, preventable contribution, not every rider-caused collision. A raised meaningful concerns about litigation uncertainty and higher fares, but repeatedly attacked automatic liability that B expressly rejected. B better explained why rider wrongdoing need not erase corporate responsibility, why regulatory fines leave compensation unresolved, and why cheaper fares do not eliminate injury costs.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B used A’s acceptance of account bans with clear triggers to identify a knowable failure: knowingly allowing a required suspension to go unenforced. A distinguished permit penalties from injury damages, but B directly answered that preventing another prohibited ride was the safeguard’s purpose; calling the subsequent misconduct independent did not resolve causation. This exchange substantially weakened A’s control and vagueness objections.</best_rebuttal>
